descriptionChirho: A masculine noun meaning footstool, always occurring in construct with 'feet' (hadom raglayim) as a compound expression for a footstool or footrest, used both literally of furniture and theologically of the earth or the temple as God's footstool (Isa 66:1; Ps 99:5, 110:1, 132:7; 1 Chr 28:2; Lam 2:1). All three clusters are purely grammatical variants (with/without conjunction waw, with/without preposition lamed): spa 'estrado de' (platform/footstool of), arb 'مَوْطِئُ/مَوْطِئَ/مَوطِئًا' (footrest), kor '발판/발받침' (footrest/footboard), swa 'kiti cha kuwekea miguu' (seat for placing feet), hin 'पावदान/चौकी' (footstool).
